subject.title: File Browser: Remove ALLOWED_FILE_NAMES whitelist, add scope levels

question: Should OpenClaw add a core Mission Control workspace/system file-browser surface beyond the existing read-only workspace-confined `agents.workspace.list/get` API, and what write or host-system scopes are allowed?
rationale: The remaining request changes the trusted operator filesystem boundary and product UX, and current policy treats high-power filesystem access as an explicit security/product decision rather than an automatic fix.

options.title: Approve workspace-read UI first
options.body: Use the existing read-only workspace-confined RPCs for a Control UI browser and keep workspace writes plus host-system browsing out until separately designed.

options.title: Sponsor full workspace CRUD
options.body: Define a new admin-scoped mutation contract with migration/proof/security requirements and use the open workspace-management issue as the canonical implementation track.

options.title: Reject host-system scope
options.body: Keep OpenClaw file browsing confined to agent workspaces and close or split any request for Windows-Explorer-style system filesystem access.

recommendation.title: Approve workspace-read UI first
recommendation.body: Use the existing read-only workspace-confined RPCs for a Control UI browser and keep workspace writes plus host-system browsing out until separately designed.

likelyOwner.reason: Most recent owner of the merged read-only workspace RPC direction and the linked mobile file-browser completion comment.
